tasks.description: Analyze the overall air quality score trend and categorize it into Good, Moderate, Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, or Hazardous levels.
Identify the main pollutant contributing to poor air quality and determine its concentration level.
Detect the peak pollution hours when air quality worsens and notify citizens accordingly.
Analyze the pollution data to infer the potential sources of pollution, such as traffic, industry, or agriculture.
Analyze the seasonal variation in pollution levels to determine if there is an increase in pollution during winter or summer months.
Map the health risks associated with pollution levels, including respiratory and cardiovascular hazards, to provide citizens with valuable insights.
Analyze the correlation between different air quality components, such as CO, NO, NO2, O3, SO2, PM2.5, and PM10, to identify potential relationships and patterns.
Analyze the spatial variation in air quality across different locations to identify areas with poor air quality and potential sources of pollution.
Analyze the diurnal variation in air quality to identify patterns and trends in pollution levels throughout the day.
Analyze the impact of weather conditions, such as temperature, humidity, and wind speed, on air quality to identify potential relationships and patterns.
Develop a forecasting model to predict future air quality levels based on historical data and trends.
Analyze the ratio of different pollutant concentrations to identify potential patterns and correlations.
Analyze the distribution of air quality index categories (e.g., Good, Moderate, Unhealthy) over time to identify trends and patterns.
Compare the pollution levels at different locations to identify areas with poor air quality and potential sources of pollution.
Analyze the temporal trends of individual pollutants (e.g., CO, NO, NO2, O3, SO2, PM2.5, PM10) to identify patterns and correlations.
Develop an alert system to notify citizens when the air quality exceeds a certain threshold, providing them with valuable insights and recommendations.
Trigger notifications when pollutant concentrations exceed threshold values, such as CO > 1000 μg/m3 or PM2.5 > 35 μg/m3.
Analyze the transition patterns between different air quality index categories (e.g., Good to Moderate, Moderate to Unhealthy) to identify common triggers and trends.
Examine the temporal autocorrelation of air quality metrics, such as daily or weekly cycles, to identify repeating patterns and correlations.
Compare the monthly average concentrations of different pollutants to identify seasonal patterns and trends, and determine if there are any significant changes over time.
Analyze the trends in pollutant concentration ratios, such as PM2.5/PM10 or NO2/NO, to identify potential changes in emission sources or atmospheric processes.
Use receptor models to estimate the contribution of different sources to pollutant concentrations, helping to identify potential pollution sources.
Apply spatial clustering algorithms to group areas with similar air quality index values, enabling the identification of pollution hotspots.
Analyze the diurnal variation of individual pollutants to identify unique patterns and correlations that can inform pollution mitigation strategies.
Decompose air quality data into trend, seasonal, and residual components to better understand the underlying patterns and relationships.
Develop exposure assessments for sensitive populations, such as children, the elderly, and those with pre-existing conditions, to provide targeted health advice.
